subject: Polity
topic: Indian Constitution — Preamble, fundamental rights, amendments

questions.stem: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with which words?
questions.explanation: Preamble: 'We, the people of India, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a Sovereign Democratic Republic...' Emphasizes popular sovereignty and democratic foundation. Trap: confusing with religious or official formulations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Preamble includes: Sovereign, Democratic, Republic, Secular (added 1976), Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity. Does NOT explicitly mention 'Parliamentary system' (though Part III/IV imply it). Answer: C. Trap: assuming all constitutional features are in Preamble.

questions.stem: When was the word 'Secular' added to the Preamble?
questions.explanation: 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Secular' and 'Socialist' to Preamble. Also added Part IVA (Fundamental Duties). Original Preamble (1950) was 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'; revised to 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic.' Trap: confusing with original Preamble or other amendments.

questions.stem: What does the term 'Sovereign' in the Preamble mean?

options.option_text: India is ruled by a King or Queen (alternative interpretation)
India has supreme power and is free from external control
India is a theocratic state (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: Sovereign: India has supreme power and autonomy in internal and external affairs. No external authority can interfere. Free from colonial rule (British dominion ended). Answer: B. Trap: A (India is not a monarchy post-1950), C (India is secular, not theocratic).

questions.stem: The Preamble aims to secure to all citizens justice, liberty, and equality. Which of these refers to 'absence of discrimination'?
questions.explanation: Equality = absence of discrimination based on caste, creed, color, religion. Liberty = freedom of expression, conscience, belief. Justice = social, economic, political fairness. Answer: C (equality = non-discrimination). Trap: confusing liberty with equality or justice.

questions.stem: What is 'Fraternity' as mentioned in the Preamble?

options.option_text: Sense of brotherliness and national integration

questions.explanation: Fraternity (from French Revolution): sense of brotherhood, national unity, and human dignity. Assures dignity of individual and unity of nation. Answer: A. Trap: limiting to religious brotherhood (B) or misinterpreting as political/economic only.

questions.stem: The Preamble is binding or merely declaratory in nature according to Indian courts?

options.option_text: Binding on all branches (legislature, executive, judiciary)
Merely declaratory; not enforceable in courts (alternative interpretation)
Binding only on the judiciary (alternative interpretation)
Binding only on the legislature (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: Supreme Court has held Preamble is binding and represents constitutional values/objectives. While not directly enforceable as law, it guides interpretation of Constitution. Acts violating Preamble can be struck down. Answer: A (binding on all branches as constitutional foundation). Trap: B (outdated view; modern jurisprudence sees Preamble as binding guide).
